ratings.plot: Things go wrong for a high ranking mobster when he doesn't follow his boss's orders.

verdict.reason: Kim Jee-woon's crime masterpiece deserves a theater. The DCP restoration at Metrograph makes the violent elegance sing.

ratings.plot: In Mumbai, Nurse Prabha's routine is troubled when she receives an unexpected gift from her estranged husband. Her younger roommate, Anu, tries in vain to find a spot in the city to be intimate with her boyfriend.

verdict.reason: Watch it. Kapadia's debut is a precise, patient film about two women in Mumbai finding small moments of freedom, shot with rare visual clarity on 35mm.

ratings.plot: In the twilight of Francisco Franco's dictatorship, an 8-year-old orphan and her two sisters find shelter in the house of their stern aunt and try their best to acclimatize to a new reality. Can they summon up the courage to grow up?

verdict.reason: Essential Saura on 35mm at a theater built for this work. A masterpiece about childhood resilience under Franco's shadow that demands the big screen.

ratings.plot: Impersonal and beautiful images of Akerman's life in New York are combined with letters from her loving but manipulative mother, read by Akerman herself.

verdict.reason: A landmark film about maternal distance and New York life—essential Akerman on the big screen. Metrograph's DCP restoration makes the spare, precise images sing.

ratings.plot: Filmed at night from Tel Aviv rooftops, this investigative documentary examines the civilian casualties of Israel's military operations in Gaza and the systems behind targeted killings of Palestinians.

verdict.reason: Essential testimony from the people who built Israel's targeting systems, shot in the dark on Tel Aviv rooftops. The 80-minute runtime keeps the weight intact without padding.

ratings.plot: Four strangers' paths cross by chance, leading to complex emotional entanglements that challenge their existing relationships and force them to confront uncomfortable truths about love and commitment.

verdict.reason: Lee Chang-dong's first film in a decade demands the big screen and your full attention. Nearly three hours of moral complexity and emotional precision—see it before word spreads.

movies.title: ONCE UPON A TIME IN HARLEM

verdict.reason: Sandra Wollner's chamber drama about grief and blame deserves the theater. The 121-minute runtime and intimate character work demand full attention on a big screen.

ratings.plot: Paul Thomas Anderson captures Brooklyn musician Cameron Winter's minimalist performance in this striking concert film, blending intimate close-ups with sweeping shots of the vast venue, all shot on 16mm and 35mm film.

verdict.reason: Paul Thomas Anderson shot a 72-minute concert film on 35mm and 16mm for a performer whose album dominated year-end lists. See it theatrical before it vanishes.

ratings.plot: A hard-partying New York City club promoter sees his whirlwind lifestyle upended by the arrival of the 10-year-old son he never knew he had.

verdict.reason: Firstman's debut balances comedy and genuine heart around an unexpected father-son story. A rare new film playing Lincoln Center that earns its two-hour runtime.

ratings.plot: A psychopath tries to forcibly persuade a tennis star to agree to his theory that two strangers can get away with murder by submitting to his plan to kill the other's most-hated person.

verdict.reason: Hitchcock's masterpiece of psychological manipulation deserves the big screen. The 35mm print at Metrograph shows why the geometry of his shot-making still cuts.

ratings.plot: An enduring, singular masterpiece of cinema starring Academy Award®-winner Vanessa Redgrave and Oliver Reed, KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is a prescient epic of obsession and corruption, and a defining work of art from seminal filmmaker Ken Russell. KEN RUSSELL’S THE DEVILS is the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience that Russell always envisioned – and the first time, the film will be presented restored and in 4K.

verdict.reason: Russell's unfiltered masterpiece demands the big screen in this definitive 4K restoration. The 2004 edit he privately constructed finally gets theatrical release as intended.

ratings.plot: A young woman suspects her neighbors have sinister plans for her pregnancy.

movies.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother

movies.title: Alamo Drafthouse x A24 Cinema Club: Pearl

ratings.plot: The allure of stardom on the big screen proves to be a road to some very dark places for Mia Goth’s titular PEARL in this stylish and gruesome prequel to Ti West’s X. With her husband away at war, Pearl finds herself dreaming of a way to escape from her boring life on the farm. She sees the silver screen as her way to find stardom and the love she so desperately needs, but her overbearing mother and her own dark impulses might hold her back from the fame she craves. PEARL proves to be a delightfully perverse study on a standout character from writer/director Ti West’s tribute to ‘70s grindhouse, X. Its vibrant, candy-coated veneer plays wonderfully against the depraved desires of the main character bubbling just below the surface. Co-writer/star Mia Goth gives another deliciously unhinged performance as Pearl, a not-quite-innocent farm girl looking for love in all the wrong places. As much a love letter to the Golden Age of Hollywood as it is a demented look at the darkness bubbling just below the surface of rural America, PEARL is colorful, unnerving, and twisted in all the right ways.

verdict.reason: Ti West's prequel is a stylish, unhinged descent into obsession and rage. Mia Goth's performance and the film's candy-colored dread make it essential theater.

ratings.plot: David Lynch blends together southern gothic melodrama, THE WIZARD OF OZ, surreal kinky violence, and Elvis in this nightmare soap opera thrill ride. Based on the pulp novel by author Barry Gifford, WILD AT HEART follows outlaw lovers Sailor (Nicolas Cage) and Lula (Laura Dern) as they go on the run through a menacing Deep South, populated by the usual stable of unsettling Lynchian weirdos (including a bonkers Willem Dafoe). Funny, scary, and brilliantly cinematic, Lynch received the Palme d’Or for this film at Cannes amid “the most violent chorus of boos and hisses to be heard in a decade.” Strap in.

verdict.reason: Lynch's Palme d'Or winner belongs on the big screen—125 minutes of southern gothic fever dream that rewards the commitment. Nicolas Cage and Laura Dern burn through every frame.

ratings.plot: Celebrate Doctor Who Day with an exclusive big-screen event marking 20 years of the Tenth Doctor and Rose Tyler. For the first time ever in cinemas, the acclaimed two-part adventure The Impossible Planet and The Satan Pit has been specially re-edited into a single movie-length presentation, created exclusively for theatrical audiences. Join the Doctor (David Tennant) and Rose (Billie Piper) as they travel to Sanctuary Base 6, a remote outpost perched on a planet orbiting a black hole. When an ancient force awakens beneath the surface, the crew find themselves trapped in a battle against an evil older than time itself. This special Doctor Who Day screening also includes exclusive bonus material, featuring previously unseen content and a brand-new interview with a special guest, reflecting on the making of one of the most celebrated stories of the modern era – from encounters with the Ood to facing the terrifying Beast, alongside behind-the-scenes memories from the set.

movies.title: Alamo Crafthouse: Wallace & Gromit: The Classic Shorts

ratings.plot: Back on the big screen for the first time in ages! Aardman Animation's beloved duo of clueless inventor Wallace and his wise, world-weary dog companion Gromit first took the world by storm in this trio of sweetly absurd Oscar-winning shorts by visionary animator Nick Park. Full of stunning filmmaking and design, clever writing and deep emotional beats, this timeless program of claymation is for the kid in us all. A GRAND DAY OUT 1989 | 25 mins. Talented but unlucky inventor Wallace travels with his loyal sidekick on a cheese-seeking moon quest. THE WRONG TROUSERS 1993 | 30 mins. Wallace’s latest invention – a pair of “Techno Trousers” – leads to danger from penguin supervillain Feathers McGraw. A CLOSE SHAVE 1995 | 30 mins. Wallace has a new invention – a Knit-O-Matic machine – and adventure looms as sheep are being rustled and poor Gromit is framed. Keep your eyes peeled for Shaun the Sheep in his big-screen debut!

But when Irwin witnesses something he wasn’t meant to see at the Gowanus Canal, the brothers find themselves pulled into a dangerous confrontation with the newly emerging Russian mafia. As the threat of violence escalates, Irwin’s wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) sounds the alarm, Irwin desperately tries to protect his family, and Gary is forced to make an impossible choice to save those he loves.

movies.title: September Songs: The Music of Kurt Weill

ratings.plot: September Songs: The Music of Kurt Weill is a fusion of film, theatre, and concert performance that reimagines the music of the German composer Kurt Weill whose songs bridged opera, cabaret, and popular music with piercing social and emotional insight. Featuring an extraordinary ensemble — Teresa Stratas, Lou Reed, Nick Cave, PJ Harvey, Charlie Haden, Elvis Costello & The Brodsky Quartet, Betty Carter, Mary Margaret O’Hara, William S. Burroughs, and more — September Songs transforms Weill’s work into a haunting collage of performance, theatre, and cinema. Each artist reinvents Weill’s legacy through their own lens, creating a living dialogue between past and present, exile and belonging, beauty and decay. Blended throughout the film are stylized “documentaries”, evocative imagery, and cinematic transitions that transform Weill’s haunting melodies and biting social commentary into a contemporary meditation on art, exile, and the human condition. The film celebrates Weill’s enduring influence on 20th-century music and culture. Through its visuals, its music and its original choreography, the film merges concert, cabaret, and expressionist cinema into a single dreamlike experience. The restoration — undertaken by Sphinx Productions with the generous support of Telefilm Canada — faithfully revives the film’s original textures, sound design, and the distinctive cinematography of celebrated German DOP Horst Zeidler, preserving a landmark of Canadian music cinema for new audiences worldwide.

Like the famed empire that Francis Ford Coppola’s epic passion project is styled after, MEGALOPOLIS is a towering, monumental spectacle that most people will think about at least once a day. The City of New Rome is at a crossroads. At one end sits Cesar Catilina (Adam Driver), the idealistic artist striving for a utopian future, and at the other sits Mayor Franklin Cicero (Giancarlo Esposito), a powerful figure perpetuating greed, special interests, and partisan warfare. Their titanic struggle will shake the foundations of their city and lay the groundwork for a new tomorrow. As engrossing and ambitious as you would expect from the filmmaker behind THE GODFATHER and APOCALYPSE NOW, MEGALOPOLIS is an unforgettable vision that could only have come from Coppola. Of course, he didn’t do it alone, and everyone in the unbelievable cast (including Driver, Esposito, Nathalie Emmanuel, Aubrey Plaza, Laurence Fishburne, and more) delivers some of the most memorable performances of their careers.

ratings.plot: “Look at that subtle off-white coloring. The tasteful thickness of it. Oh, my God. It even has a watermark.” Before Christian Bale was the savior of Gotham, he was the chainsaw-wielding, business card-slinging scourge of Manhattan. Caught during the height of American Yuppieism in the late '80s, Patrick Bateman finds himself surrounded by friends who he hates and a culture he can’t stand. Can anyone blame him for allowing his nightly bloodlust to overflow into the day? It’s hard to imagine anyone aside from Bale lecturing a soon-to-be victim on the cultural undertones found within Huey Lewis and The News’ “Hip to be Square,” all while wearing a raincoat and holding an incredibly shiny axe. But, what now seems meant to be almost wasn’t! The role was originally offered to none other than Leonardo DiCaprio. However, due to his newfound fame within the teenaged female demographic, Leo’s managers felt that a stint as a sociopathic mass murderer might somehow taint his image. I guess a career in murders and executions isn’t for everyone. Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have to return some videotapes.

Presented in an English dub In modern-day Tokyo, three homeless people’s lives are changed forever when they discover a baby girl at a garbage dump on Christmas Eve. As the New Year fast approaches, these three forgotten members of society band together to solve the mystery of the abandoned child and the fate of her parents. Along the way, encounters with seemingly unrelated events and people force them to confront their own haunted pasts, as they learn to face their future, together. Co-written by Keiko Nobumoto ( Cowboy Bebop ) and featuring a whimsical score by Keiichi Suzuki, TOKYO GODFATHERS is a masterpiece by turns heartfelt, hilarious, and highly original, a tale of hope and redemption in the face of seemingly insurmountable odds. (GKIDS)

Imagine any artist's worst nightmare of running into a crazed "#1 fan" who takes you hostage and forces you to "dance like a monkey" to play out their own sadistic fantasies. Maybe Stephen King was thinking about this when writing MISERY, a book and movie about a famous author (James Caan) who gets into a violent car accident and is then saved, coincidentally, by his "#1 fan." What unfolds is an absolute nightmare of seclusion, captivity, and abuse that reaches a boiling climax of white-knuckle suspense! This is easily one of the best King adaptions.

ratings.plot: Exploding with day-glo visuals and over-the-top gallows humor, THE TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE 2 is not what audiences expected from recovering wunderkind Tobe Hooper in 1986. But that’s exactly what makes it so special. Using the surreal terror of the first movie as a jumping off point, TEXAS CHAINSAW MASSACRE 2 plays out like a deranged form of vaudeville with Leatherface as a sexually frustrated straight-man. Featuring electric performances from Bill “Chop Top” Moseley, Caroline Williams, and a chainsaw-wielding Dennis Hopper, it’s time to praise this movie for what it is—a drop-dead masterpiece of subversive 1980s horror. (American Genre Film Archive)

Based on the true story of one of America's greatest unsolved mysteries of one of its most notorious serial killers, ZODIAC is as much a story of obsession as it is a story of murder. In the ‘60s and ‘70s, the Zodiac was a serial killer in the San Francisco area who would routinely taunt the police with letters and ciphers in newspapers. One day, a young political cartoonist, Robert Graysmith (Jake Gyllenhaal), cracks one of the Zodiac’s ciphers and spirals into a sea of perpetual preoccupation with solving his riddles and finding out his true identity with the help of his co-worker/crime reporter friend Paul Avery (Robert Downey Jr.). Always intrigued by the case while growing up in the Bay Area, the Zodiac was David Fincher’s “ultimate boogeyman.” Fincher set out with his screenwriter and producer to conduct an 18-month investigation into the unsolved case while rewriting the screenplay. The result is the story of a reporter determined to get the story at any cost. New to being an investigative reporter, he becomes all-consumed by his obsession to know the truth. Somehow along the way, it seems as though Fincher and company got caught up in that compulsion and created a spectacularly layered, investigative, and riveting narrative in their attempt to find a culprit posthumously. This film was a technical marvel and a true cinematic masterpiece of Fincher’s career that, despite overwhelming positive reviews and an all-star cast, was left basically ignored by audiences. Don’t make the same mistake twice and miss your chance to get swept up in this gut-wrenching sea of anxiety!

Marina Pinares, the wife of the president of a South American country, insists on being his vice-presidential running mate in the next election. She's no stranger to assassination to get what she wants, so some suspect she'll kill her own husband after the election to become president. In a series of flashbacks we see her rise to power: a party girl willing to sacrifice a friend's virtue to gain favor; the lover of a soldier she later tortures; the mistress of the military man she soon marries. Based on the life of Eva Peron and directed by adult filmmaker Radley Metzger (SCORE, THE OPENING OF MISTY BEETHOVEN), LITTLE MOTHER is a rarely-seen tale of political intrigue that's ready for rediscovery.
